So, 30 fifths fit into 6. This means that when you divide 6 into fifths, you get 30 fifths.
backend_description: Six pink rectangles 2 rows of 3. Each rectangle has 4 vertical dashed lines dividing it into 5 equal sections, representing fifths. This appears to be a template for students to shade or work with fractions involving fifths.
